FN-HGR9A88-1
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 140
Committee: Education Policy Sponsor: Senator J.T. 'Jabo' Waggoner
Analyst: Tiffany Weaver Date: 02/18/2025
Senate Bill 140 as introduced would increase the obligations of the Alabama Department of
Public Health (ADPH) to implement, administer, and enforce compliance of youth athletic
associations with the Coach Safely Act, by the following amounts: (1) an undetermined amount
for salaries and benefits and other personnel related expenditures dependent on the method
(digitally or in-person) chosen by ADPH to enforce compliance; (2) a department estimated
$85,000 for the first year, and $35,000 annually thereafter, to develop a compliance tracking
system to monitor the associations for compliance; and (3) a department estimated $50,000
annually to print, mail and distribute noncompliance notifications.
In addition, this bill could increase receipts by an undetermined amount to the State General
Fund dependent on the number of youth athletic associations that are noncompliant for three
consecutive years and are assessed a fine equal to 10% of the their total revenues reported to the
IRS.

FN-HGR9A88-3
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 140
Committee: Children and Senior Advocacy Sponsor: Senator J.T. 'Jabo' Waggoner
Analyst: Tiffany Weaver Date: 03/18/2025
Senate Bill 140 as passed the Senate would increase the obligations of the Alabama Department
of Public Health (ADPH) to enforce compliance of youth athletic associations with the existing
Coach Safely Act, by the following amounts: (1) an undetermined amount for personnel-related
expenditures, dependent on the method (digitally or in-person) chosen by ADPH to enforce
compliance; (2) a department-estimated $85,000 for the first year, and $35,000 annually
thereafter, to develop a compliance tracking system to monitor compliance; and (3) a
department-estimated $50,000 annually to print and distribute noncompliance notifications.
In addition, this bill could increase receipts to the State General Fund by an undetermined
amount dependent on the number of youth athletic associations that are assessed a fine equal to
10% of the association's prior year revenues, as reported to the IRS.

FN-HGR9A88-4
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 140
Committee: Children and Senior Advocacy Sponsor: Senator J.T. 'Jabo' Waggoner
Analyst: Tiffany Weaver Date: 03/19/2025
Senate Bill 140 as passed the Committee on Children and Senior Advocacy would increase the
obligations of the Alabama Department of Public Health (ADPH) to enforce compliance of
youth athletic associations with the existing Coach Safely Act, by the following amounts: (1) an
undetermined amount for personnel-related expenditures, dependent on the method (digitally or
in-person) chosen by ADPH to enforce compliance; (2) a department-estimated $85,000 for the
first year, and $35,000 annually thereafter, to develop a compliance tracking system to monitor
compliance; and (3) a department-estimated $50,000 annually to print and distribute
noncompliance notifications.
In addition, this bill could increase receipts to the State General Fund by an undetermined
amount dependent on the number of youth athletic associations that are assessed a fine as
follows: (1) $200 dollars for those associations that have less than 100 coaches, or (2) $10 per
coach for those associations with 100 or more coaches.
